calibration.method: ordinary least squares of logit(no-vig market probability) on the Valve Regional Standings point delta, through the origin; S = sum(delta^2) / sum(delta * logit)

rules.name: Maximum-probability pick (default)
rules.text: Because points are flat per correct pick, expected points = offered_points x P(win). The leaderboard-optimal pick is always the higher-probability side of our independent line. Fading the crowd earns no bonus.

rules.name: Free contrarian (information edge)
rules.text: Where our line's favourite is NOT the crowd's favourite, R1 and contrarianism point the same way: take the higher-probability side and collect the ownership differential for free. These are the only contrarian picks this desk calls 'climb' picks by default.
rules.gate: our pick probability >= 50% AND crowd ownership of our pick <= 40%

rules.name: Verified-context swing (labelled, capped)
rules.text: A sub-50% side may be taken only with two or more independently verified context flags (roster change / onboarding, head-to-head inside 30 days, rest or schedule, in-event form swing) AND a market price at or above the break-even decimal for our own fair probability. Maximum two per day, and only on fixtures worth 3 points or more.
rules.gate: our probability >= 30% (the 'not stupid' floor) AND >= 2 verified context flags AND offered decimal >= 1/our probability
rules.cost: negative EV versus R1; variance only

rules.name: Variance play when behind (explicit, not recommended by default)
rules.text: Hotspawn's prizes go to the top 10 and the board resets weekly. A player trailing the 10th place score late in the week can only close the gap with variance, so a small number of R3 swings is rational for that player and irrational for the leader. The gap and the number of picks left are user-side inputs we do not have, so this rule is published as a decision aid, never auto-applied.
rules.gate: user is behind the prize cut with few picks left

rules.name: Streak protection
rules.text: HotSpawn awards bonus points for consecutive correct picks but does not publish the bonus value, so it cannot be optimised. Until it is quantified the desk treats it as a tie-breaker only: between two picks of equal probability, prefer the one that keeps an existing streak alive (the higher-probability side).

rules: Picks lock 5 minutes before the scheduled start time (also published per fixture by the API: lock_offset_sec = 360).
'Earn points for every correct pick. Higher tier matches reward more points.' No ownership-scaled payout is published.
'Get bonus points for consecutive correct picks. The longer your streak, the bigger the bonus.' The bonus value is not published.
Forfeited match: all predictions voided, no points awarded or deducted.
Cancelled match: all predictions cancelled, no points, excluded from the leaderboard.

flags.title: HotSpawn's published scoring has no ownership term, so 'points x (probability - crowd ownership)' differentials are not a payout model
flags.detail: The official how-it-works page states only 'Earn points for every correct pick. Higher tier matches reward more points' plus an unquantified consecutive-correct streak bonus, and the fixtures API points model exposes exactly five multipliers (game, tier, series, stage, tournament) with no ownership field. Several boards already published in this repository rank contrarian value by points x (probability - crowd ownership). That formula implies a payout that HotSpawn does not publish. This desk therefore ranks picks by expected points = offered_points x probability, and treats ownership purely as context.

flags.title: The TWC Malta day-4 semi-finals are not pickable on HotSpawn
flags.detail: The HotSpawn fixtures API returns an empty list for competition 35859 with status=scheduled, and its unfiltered competition response contains only the eleven group-stage/decider rows — no semi-final, third-place or grand-final row. The website schedule does carry 17 Oct rows 1080207 (14:00 UTC, FURIA v 'Waiting for information') and 1080208 (17:00 UTC, Falcons v 'Waiting for information'), and 18 Oct rows at 11:30 UTC and 15:00 UTC with both sides 'Waiting for information'. So day 4's leaderboard points come entirely from the 7 non-TWC lobby fixtures (20 points available), not from the semi-finals. The collector re-checks competition 35859 every run and will pick the semi-finals up automatically if HotSpawn lists them.
sources: HotSpawn fixtures API, competition 35859, all statuses (11 rows, none a semi-final)

flags.title: HotSpawn's tournament page still shows settled day-3 matches as LIVE / UPCOMING
flags.detail: Read this session, the tournament page rendered Aurora v 9z (1080205) as LIVE and BetBoom v Legacy (1081775) as UPCOMING, while the fixtures API reports both as status='ended' with scores 2-0 and 2-1. Settlement and status disagree inside HotSpawn itself; the API is treated as authoritative for results.

flags.title: offered_points does not equal base_points x the published multipliers
flags.detail: Tier S: base 2 with game 1.25 and tier 3 multipliers gives 7.5, but the API publishes offered_points 7. Tier B: 2 x 1.25 x 1.5 = 3.75 but offered_points is 3. Both are consistent with truncation to an integer, but HotSpawn publishes no rounding rule, so the values are recorded verbatim and the rounding is labelled a hypothesis, never applied to any calculation.
sources: HotSpawn fixtures API rows 1080176 (tier s) and 1081888 (tier b)

flags.title: Official Valve VRS and HLTV's live ranking disagree on the SF1 favourite's ordering
flags.detail: The official Valve global standings snapshot 2026_10_05 rank FURIA #7 on 1829 points and Aurora #9 on 1716 (FURIA +113). HLTV's match analytics for 2399414 ranks FURIA #4 and Aurora #6 in its own world ranking. Boards published earlier in this repository also cite an 'HLTV live Valve-VRS forecast' of Aurora 1848 (#5) over FURIA 1824 (#6). Three orderings, two of them putting Aurora ahead. This desk originates its model line from the official Valve file only, states the snapshot date on every row, and does not merge the HLTV numbers into it.

flags.title: HotSpawn's semi-final preview quotes VRS ranks that match neither the official Valve file nor HLTV
flags.detail: HotSpawn's own preview states 'On VRS, the difference between the two teams is significant, with Falcons ranked 4th and BetBoom 12th'. The official Valve global standings 2026_10_05 list Falcons #6 (1843) and BETBOOM #11 (1596); HLTV's October 12 world ranking lists Falcons #5. The HotSpawn figures are recorded as HotSpawn's claim and are not used as a probability input (HotSpawn is discovery and settlement only in this project).

flags.title: One team, three names across sources (BET-M / 33 Team / thirtythree)
flags.detail: HotSpawn fixture 1079170 lists 'BET-M v Just Players' at 2026-10-17T08:00:00Z. bo3.gg match 131171 has slug 'thirtythree-vs-just-players-17-10-2026', team1_id 22191 and bet_updates.team_1.name 'BET-M' at the same 08:00:00Z. Melbet's LineFeed lists '33 Team v Just Players' with start epoch 1792233000 = 2026-10-17T10:30:00Z, two and a half hours later. The join rule (start within 90 minutes and a name match) therefore rejects the Melbet row and flags it instead of silently pricing the wrong match. No alias is asserted beyond the bo3.gg slug/name pair, which is the same record.

flags.title: The lobby's weekly-reset countdown and its own fixture list disagree
flags.detail: Read at 2026-10-16T23:53Z the lobby showed 'Resets in 2d 00h 10m 03s' (implying a reset around 2026-10-19T00:03Z) while still listing fixtures that start on 19 and 20 October as part of 'this week' (159 matches). Which week the 19-20 October fixtures score into is not stated anywhere official, so the day-4 desk counts points only for fixtures that start before the observed reset and labels the rest as next-week-uncertain.

flags.title: HotSpawn listed a cancelled TWC fixture that 33 players had already picked
flags.detail: Fixture 1080204 (Legacy v FURIA, day 2) is status='cancelled' with total_picks 33 and ownership 30%/70%; the replayed fixture 1081614 settled 1-2 with total_picks 0 and 0%/0% ownership. Per the official rules a cancelled match awards no points, so 33 players lost a pickable 7-point fixture through no fault of their own and nobody could pick the replay. Recorded because it is a real, if unlucky, hole in day-2 coverage.
sources: HotSpawn how it works — cancelled matches
